enquiry: Our juice bottling line sometimes fills batches that customers describe as tasting off. We were told UV/Vis spectroscopy is extremely sensitive, so we want to put it on the filler and let it reject bad batches automatically. We do not know what causes the off taste.

clarification_questions.question: What goes wrong today when a batch tastes off: how is it detected, what does it cost you, and what decision should real-time data drive on the filler?
clarification_questions.why: Clarifies the pain and whether an automatic reject decision is the right goal.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Off-taste batches are detected late by customers; the decision to be supported is unclear, so lab screening will first establish the cause.

clarification_questions.question: Do you know, or suspect, which compound or property causes the off taste, and at what level does it become noticeable?
clarification_questions.why: Determines whether UV/Vis can see the target at all and whether ppm or % level is needed.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Target unknown; level unknown. Lab screening establishes whether the target is ppm or % level and whether UV/Vis responds to it.

clarification_questions.question: Is the juice clear, turbid or opaque at the filler, and does its appearance vary between batches?
clarification_questions.why: Optical state decides the probe geometry (transmission, transflection or ATR) and whether UV/Vis light reaches the detector.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Juice assumed clear liquid; turbidity variation unknown and must be checked in lab screening.

clarification_questions.question: How does the juice vary along the process (fruit source, pasteurisation, temperature, cleaning cycles, pulp or bubbles), and when in the run do off-taste batches occur?
clarification_questions.why: Shows whether variation comes from the juice itself or from the line, which affects whether a sensor on the filler can be representative.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Variation sources unknown; batches are assumed to differ in composition, and time-aligned samples are needed.

clarification_questions.question: Where exactly would the probe sit on the filler, and is there space and access for a probe and any fiber link to the analyzer?
clarification_questions.why: Defines the installation point, distance to the analyzer and whether a fiber type compatible with the wavelength range is needed.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Installation point not defined; no fiber or distance assumed until the layout is known.

clarification_questions.question: How is off taste confirmed today (sensory panel, lab chemistry, customer complaints), and how accurate is that method?
clarification_questions.why: A reference method is needed to test whether any optical signal correlates with off taste.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: No reference method known; a sensory or lab reference must be set up before any sensor claim is tested.

clarification_questions.question: What accuracy, response time and budget do you need for an automatic reject decision, and what is the cost of a false reject or a missed bad batch?
clarification_questions.why: Sets the requirements that decide whether a single UV/Vis method is sufficient or another method is needed.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Requirements unknown; the simplest single-method option will be tested first in lab screening.

flags_before_revision.detail: different_context: S01 p.5 says UV-visible spectroscopy has very high sensitivity especially in the UV region (190-360 nm), which supports the claim; however the table (TABLE:r13) rates cuvette UV/Vis sensitivity high while probe rows rate it low, so the unqualified claim transfers a lab/cuvette-type rating to the process setting without saying so. Fix: Say UV/Vis is rated highly sensitive in the UV region for cuvette measurements (TABLE:r13), while probe-based UV/Vis rows are rated low sensitivity.

not_supported: The cited pages rate UV/Vis selectivity low, but the claim's statement about the in-line transmission probe row being low sensitivity is a mismatch in scope: the page lists several probe rows, and the note that sensitivity alone does not show identification of an unknown cause is not stated by any cited page. Fix: Limit the claim to the table ratings (selectivity low; transmission probe sensitivity low per TABLE:r16) and drop the unsupported inference about identifying unknown causes.

different_context: The quoted bioprocess text on UV-Transmission probes concerns bioprocess media with path lengths of 1-10 mm; applying it to juice clarity transfers it to a different sample type without saying so. Fix: State that the support is from bioprocess media and that transfer to juice is untested.

overstated: Stating UV/Vis is useful only if the cause absorbs is a reasonable limit, but the cited table cells are generic ratings and do not establish the conclusion for off-taste detection. Fix: Frame it as a conditional assumption requiring lab confirmation rather than a rule derived from the table.

not_supported: S02 p.6 lists UV-VIS silica fibers at 190-1200 nm and VIS-NIR silica at 350-2400 nm; the claim that Vis-NIR silica covers NIR to 2.4 um is accurate, but the claim that UV-Vis silica covers UV/Vis is only a nominal fiber range, not an instrument range, which the brief forbids treating as a specific instrument range. Fix: Describe these as nominal fiber transmission ranges and note that the actual instrument and probe range must be confirmed.

not_supported: S01 p.16 mentions saturation from turbidity and opacity but does not mention pulp or bubbles mimicking composition changes. Fix: Limit the risk to turbidity-driven saturation as stated on the page and mark pulp and bubble effects as unsourced assumptions.

rule_hints: nominal_range_not_instrument_range: A nominal method range is not the usable range of a specific instrument, fiber or probe. [DOCX §3; DOCX §5]

geometry_follows_optics: Clear liquids suit transmission or transflection; opaque, concentrated or powder samples suit diffuse reflection; highly absorbing or 'black' liquids suit ATR. [S01 Table 1 (p.6); S01 p.16; S01 p.17-18]
do_not_invent: Do not invent measured results, accuracy, detection limits, response times, fiber lengths, product codes or prices, client facts, or guarantees. [DOCX §3]
insufficient_information_is_valid: If the known facts cannot justify a method choice, say so, ask the deciding questions and propose the next step. [DOCX §3]
